skills.trigger: When evaluating a pleural-based mass on chest CT to distinguish malignant mesothelioma from benign pleural disease or intrapulmonary lesions.
steps: Inspect the pleural surface of the mass for nodularity, lobulation, or irregular thickening rather than a smooth contour.
Assess the extent of the lesion to determine if it involves the mediastinal pleura or encases thoracic structures, indicating aggressive behavior.
Differentiate from benign etiologies by noting the absence of discrete calcifications and the presence of diffuse, invasive growth patterns.

skills.trigger: When determining the anatomical origin (intrapulmonary vs. extrapulmonary/pleural) of a chest wall abutting mass.
steps: Evaluate the angle formed between the mass and the chest wall; an obtuse angle suggests an extrapulmonary (pleural) origin.
Contrast this with an acute angle, which typically indicates an intrapulmonary lesion arising from the lung parenchyma.
Use this geometric relationship to support the classification of the mass as pleural-based before assessing specific malignant features.
